SMTO-SKL-0053 — Google Drive refused this request

GUID: 16ad0622-1f77-5c8d-aa6c-fa49b17bf73e
Slug: google-drive-provider-rejected
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • Google Drive turned down what SMTO asked it to do and didn't say it was a sign-in, permission or missing-file problem. SMTO did not try the request again on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Google Drive in your browser and try the same action yourself on the same file, for example sharing it or renaming it. Google shows its own reason on screen, which tells you what it won't allow for this file.
  2. If you asked SMTO to change something, check in Google Drive whether the change already appears before asking for it again. SMTO never repeats a change on its own, so checking first prevents doing it twice.
  3. Ask SMTO again with a simpler or corrected request, such as a different file name, a different person to share with, or a different folder. Google refuses requests that break its own rules for that file, so changing the request is what gets past it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the result you asked for, and Google Drive shows the same thing.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Google Workspace. Don't share your Google password, sign-in links or file contents.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive returned a non-success status that is not one of the recognized sign-in, permission, not-found, conflict, rate-limit or server-failure cases.

What this means

  • Drive returns a non-success status outside its recognized authentication, permission, resource, conflict, quota and server-failure classes. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Drive returns a non-success status outside its recognized authentication, permission, resource, conflict, quota and server-failure classes.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual status and supported operation constraints.

How to fix it

  • Read the http_status in the diagnostic details (typically a 400-class status mapped by provider_error in skills/google_drive/client.py) and compare the requested operation with Google Drive API limits for that file type, name, permission or shared drive. Correct the request; no write was replayed automatically, so verify the file's current state before issuing another change.
  • Review the requested operation and provider constraints; no write has been automatically replayed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the requested operation and provider constraints; no write has been automatically replayed.

How to verify the fix

  • A corrected deliberate request succeeds or its specific provider limitation is reported.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
